1. Executive Summary & Investment Thesis

SEDEMAC Mechatronics Limited is India's preeminent deep-tech automotive electronics innovator, pioneering globally patented sensorless control technologies for Integrated Starter Generators (ISGs), Electric Vehicle Motor Control Units (MCUs), and industrial engine governors. Founded out of an IIT Bombay research incubation lab, the company possesses an elite R&D DNA that replaces fragile hardware sensors with proprietary mathematical algorithms.

Core Thesis Pillars:
• Explosive Operating Leverage: Audited EBITDA grew 4.1× from ₹54.2 Cr (FY23) to ₹222.2 Cr (FY26), with PAT exploding 12.1× to ₹103.6 Cr as fixed R&D costs scaled.
• Massive EV Content Multiplier: Moving from ICE starter ECUs (~₹1,200) to EV Traction Motor Controllers (₹8,000–₹12,000) drives a 7×–10× content expansion per vehicle across TVS, Hero, and Bajaj.
• Sovereign Float Absorption: On September 24, 2026, a ₹1,468 Crore block deal cleanly transferred early PE ownership (A91 & Xponentia) into sovereign wealth funds (GIC Singapore ₹308 Cr, MAS ₹71 Cr) and premier domestic MFs (SBI MF ₹358 Cr, Invesco MF ₹307 Cr) at ₹3,010.00.

8. Proprietary Patent Estate, Workforce & Future Pipeline

SEDEMAC owns an estate of over 80+ patents across India, the US, Europe, Japan, and China. Its core competitive differentiator is the sensorless motor control algorithm that computes rotor position via phase voltage/current feedback rather than relying on failure-prone Hall sensors.

  • R&D Talent Base: ~700–850 employees, with over 60% dedicated to embedded firmware, power electronics, and control theory.
  • High-Voltage EV Traction MCUs (Upcoming): 48V–150V silicon-carbide (SiC) inverters for high-speed e-motorcycles and e-LCVs (₹8,000–₹12,000 realization).
  • Smart ISG 2.0 (Mild Hybrid): Combines starter-generator with regenerative braking and torque assist for ICE scooters (+10% fuel economy).
  • CPCB-IV+ Hybrid Genset Controllers: Next-generation digital controllers integrating solar PV, battery storage, and diesel engines for telecom/data centers.

9. Defense Footprint & Tactical Dual-Use Assessment

While SEDEMAC reports no separate defense segment, its core technologies directly penetrate indirect defense supply chains and tactical dual-use systems:

  • Tactical Auxiliary Power Units (APUs): Primary supplier of electronic engine governors and GCUs to Cummins and Kirloskar Oil Engines (KOEL), powering auxiliary generator units for T-90 / Arjun tanks and mobile radar shelters.
  • High-Altitude UAV & Drone Electronics: Tactical drones and loitering munitions require Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI) capable of barometric density adaptation in high-altitude environments (Ladakh, Siachen) and fail-safe sensorless motor commutation.
  • MoD Indigenization Tailwinds: The Ministry of Defence’s Positive Indigenization lists bar unverified Chinese ECUs; SEDEMAC’s 100% domestic IP and Pune manufacturing offer a secure, sovereign electronics alternative.

10. Pricing Power & Chinese Competition Moat

  • Cost Pass-Through Resilience: Despite global semiconductor inflation, SEDEMAC expanded EBITDA margins by 990 bps. Tier-1 contracts feature quarterly indexation clauses passing raw material and chip cost variances to OEMs.
  • Why Chinese Vendors Cannot Dislodge SEDEMAC: (1) Chinese competitors rely on fragile Hall-sensor hardware; SEDEMAC owns the patented sensorless IP. (2) Indian EV regulations (PLI / EMPS / Phased Manufacturing Program) require >50% domestic value addition, penalizing Chinese imports with 15–20% customs duties. (3) Tier-1 OEMs (TVS, Hero, Bajaj) require 24–36 months of ARAI compliance testing and refuse unverified foreign electronics.
  • Western "China+1" Beneficiary: US Section 301 tariffs (25–50%) on Chinese electronics are driving Western OEMs (Generac, Cummins, Kohler) to source genset controls directly from SEDEMAC India.

13. Key Investment Risks (Bear Case Analysis)

  • Multiple De-rating Risk: At 116× trailing P/E, any single quarter of delayed OEM deliveries or flat earnings will trigger short-term multiple compression.
  • Customer Concentration: Top 3 Indian 2W OEMs (TVS, Hero, Bajaj) account for >65% of revenues. OEM-specific volume swings directly impact quarterly earnings.
  • EV Adoption Pacing: If Indian electric two-wheeler adoption decelerates due to reduced government subsidies, high-ASP MCU volume ramp could be delayed.
